section_title: Criteria for Designation of Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises (SSDEs)
chapter: Chapter II - Regulation of Core Digital Services
section_text: The Competition Commission of India shall designate an enterprise as a Systemically Significant Digital Enterprise (SSDE) in respect of a Core Digital Service if it meets the quantitative thresholds prescribed under Section 4 or meets the qualitative criteria prescribed under Section 5. An enterprise so designated shall comply with all ex-ante regulatory obligations set out in this Chapter.

chapter: Chapter II - Regulation of Core Digital Services
section_text: An enterprise shall be designated as an SSDE if in India: (a) its turnover exceeds INR 4,000 crore, or global turnover exceeds USD 30 billion; or (b) its gross merchandise value exceeds INR 16,000 crore; and (c) its core digital service has not less than 1 crore end-users or 10,000 business users in India over the preceding three financial years.

section_title: Qualitative Factors for Determining Systemic Significance
chapter: Chapter II - Regulation of Core Digital Services
section_text: Even if an enterprise does not satisfy the quantitative criteria in Section 4, the Commission may designate it as an SSDE having regard to: (a) market volume and network effects; (b) financial strength and access to capital; (c) vertical integration; (d) user lock-in and switching costs; and (e) ability to influence market dynamics across allied services.

section_title: Obligations of Associate Enterprises and Corporate Groups
chapter: Chapter II - Regulation of Core Digital Services
section_text: Where an enterprise is designated as an SSDE, the Commission may extend obligations to its associate enterprises, subsidiaries, and group companies if they operate interrelated digital services or share user data across distinct operational divisions.

section_title: General Obligations and Code of Fair Conduct
section_text: Every SSDE shall conduct its business in a fair, non-discriminatory, and transparent manner with business users and end users. No SSDE shall engage in unfair contract terms, arbitrary termination of merchant accounts, or discriminatory algorithmic ranking.

An SSDE shall not prevent, restrict, or discourage business users from communicating with, promoting offers to, or directing end users to purchase products or services outside the SSDE's core digital service, nor shall it impose discriminatory charges for external transactions.

section_title: Prohibition on Self-Preferencing and Search Bias
section_text: An SSDE shall not, directly or indirectly, favor its own products, services, private labels, or related entity offerings over those of competing third-party business users on its platform in search rankings, placement, or recommendation algorithms.

section_title: Restrictions on Data Cross-Use, Profiling and Merchant Data Exploitation
section_text: An SSDE shall not use non-public commercial data generated by business users on its platform to compete against them. Furthermore, an SSDE shall not cross-use, combine, or profile personal data of end users collected from different services without explicit, freely given consent.

section_title: Interoperability Requirements for Core Digital Platforms
section_text: An SSDE shall ensure technical interoperability of complementary hardware, software, or operating system features with third-party providers on fair and equivalent conditions, without degrading system stability or security unnecessarily.

section_title: Allowing Third-Party Application Stores and Direct Sideloading
section_text: An SSDE operating an operating system or application marketplace shall allow end users to install and effectively use third-party applications and alternative app stores, and shall not restrict users from selecting alternative default payment or web browsing services.

section_title: Dedicated Dispute Redressal and Compliance Officer
section_text: Every SSDE shall establish an independent, transparent grievance redressal mechanism within India, headed by a designated Chief Compliance Officer, and shall resolve business user grievances within fifteen days.

section_title: Penalties for Contravention of Ex-Ante Obligations
section_text: If the Commission finds that an SSDE has contravened any obligation under this Act, it may impose a monetary penalty not exceeding ten percent of the global turnover of the enterprise for each contravention, in addition to ordering structural behavioral remedies or divestment.
